newsitem.title: USA: Yahoo tops estimates, cash-flow positive.
newsitem.headline: Yahoo tops estimates, cash-flow positive.

text.p: Internet directory company Yahoo! Inc defied Wall Street's expectations of a fourth-quarter loss, posting a modest profit in the period and scoring its first cash flow positive quarter ever.
The company on Tuesday reported its revenues rose 55 percent over the third quarter to $8.5 million in the period ended December 31, 1996.
Net income was $96,000, or $0.00 per share, compared with a net income of $92,000 a year earlier.
Wall Street had expected the company to turn in a loss, with consensus estimates at five cents a share, according to First Call's survey of analyst estimates.

Yahoo! Chief Financial Officer Gary Valenzuela said the company turned cash flow positive, with a $1.5 million net cash flow in the quarter, as total page views including Yahoo! Japan rose to 20 million a day in the month of December.
This was up from over 15 million a day in September, including Yahoo! Japan, which, on its own, amounted to about a million page views per day in September and 1.4 million in December.
Valenzuela said the company expects to continue to grow its business aggressively along its strategy of expanding its geographic, demographic and subject area properties.

"We're going to emphasise growth," he said in an interview. "We're focused on building long-term value for shareholders, particularly at this early stage, growing market share and building out the Yahoo! family of properties."

"We're going to emphasise growth and it's going to be growth in a number of metrics -- revenues, traffic, scanning the properties, getting in front of as many eyeballs as possible, and leveraging the brand," he added.
Yahoo!'s advertiser base increased to 550 in the fourth quarter, up from 340 in the third quarter, adding a combination of consumer brands and technology companies.
